------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Genome quantification, preparation, and cleanup

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Nextera XT Sample Preparation

Samples submitted for small genome sequencing should be quantified via the [Qubit](#qubitsample), and use the [Nextera XT Kit]{style="color:#009900"} for preparation and clean up

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Nextera XT Acronyms and Method Overview

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

| **Acronym** | **Definition**            |
|:------------|:--------------------------|
| TD          | Tagment DNA Buffer        |
| ATM         | Amplicon Tagment Mix      |
| NT          | Neutralize Tagment Buffer |
| NPM         | Nextera PCR Master Mix    |

```{r, out.width = "50%", echo=FALSE, fig.align='left'}
knitr::include_graphics("https://i0.wp.com/www.molecularecologist.com/wp-content/uploads/2015/01/Screen-Shot-2015-01-20-at-12.48.12-AM.png?resize=468%2C533")
```

$\tiny \text{    A. Nextera XT transposome with partial adapters is combined with template DNA Call out}$   $\tiny \text{    B. Tagmentation to fragment and add partial adapters}$   $\tiny \text{    C. Limited cycle PCR to add sequencing primer sequences and indexes}$

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Nextera XT Sample Preparation - Workflow

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

Multiple reagents must be pulled out of the freezer ahead of time. *Tagment Reagents* $\rightarrow$ **ATM** & **TD** reagents must be thawed on ice\
Pull these reagents out before starting the reactions.

*Amplification Reagents* $\rightarrow$ Indices must be thawed at room temperature. **NPM** reagent must be thawed on ice.\
Pull these reagents out after placing the samples in the thermocycler for the tagmentation step.

1.  Quantify submitted DNA using the [Qubit]{style="color:#009900"}, then dilute to **0.2ng/μL**\
    *Concentrations between 0.17ng/μL and 0.3ng/μL are acceptable*

2.  Use **2.5μL of the \~0.2ng/μL dilution** to enter into the Nextera XT preparation kit.\
    Reactions can be completed in 0.5mL PCR tubes, strips, or a 96 well semi skirted plate, depending on the number of genomes to be prepared.

3.  Add **5μL** of [**TD**]{style="color:#009900"} to each sample and pipette to mix

4.  Add **2.5μL** of [**ATM**]{style="color:#009900"} to each sample and pipette to mix

5.  Place the plate in [Thermocycler CT019662]{style="color:#009900"}\
    Use protocol [**NEXTERA_TAG**]{style="color:#4d53da"} found in the [\<**Root**\>]{style="color:#4d53da"} folder

6.  Upon completion, **immediately** remove the plate from the thermocycler

7.  Add **2.5μL** of [**NT**]{style="color:#009900"} and pipette to mix.\
    Quickly centrifuge the plate and incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes.

8.  Add **7.5μL** [**NPM**]{style="color:#009900"} to each sample.

9.  Add **2.5μL of the Forward Primer** and **2.5μL of the Reverse Primer** and pipette to mix.\
    Centrifuge briefly.

    Be mindful when selecting Indices, especially when working with just a handful of samples.

    Illumina recommends the following:

```{r, echo=FALSE, Warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
numbsmp<-c("2 Samples","3 Samples","4-5 Samples","6 Samples")
Ri7<- c("N702 & N701 **or** N702 & N704","N701, N702, & N704 **or** N703, N705 & N706","N701, N702, N704, & any 1 additional **or** N703, N705, N706, & any 1 additional","N701, N702, N703, N704, N705, & N706")
Fi5 <- c("Any","Any","Any","Any")
illprimers<- data.frame(numbsmp,Ri7,Fi5)
colnames(illprimers) <- c("Number of Samples", "Reverse (i7) Primer Selection", "Forward(i5) Primer Selection")
knitr::kable(illprimers, align = "l", booktabs=T) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = c("striped", "bordered"), full_width = F, position = "left")
```

    **<span style ="color:#4d53da">NOTE</span>: i7 indexes are not repeated unless completely necessary**
      

1.  Place the plate in [**Thermocycler CT019662**]{style="color:#009900"}.\
    Use protocol [**NEXTERA_PCR**]{style="color:#4d53da"} found in the [\<**Root**\>]{style="color:#4d53da"}folder

    You may stop at this point.\
    **Do not proceed with library normalization or sequencing protocol as written in the Nextera Protocol**

2.  PCR clean-up and size select amplified tagments as outlined above\
    Use the Mag-Beads found in the 4C fridge\
    Use the Alpaqua Magnum FLX magnet to clear the supernatant

3.  Genomes should be brought to 4nM (1.7ng/μL) for sequencing using the Qubit

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## TruSeq PCR-Free Sample Preparation

Concentrate samples to \~40 ng/μL (35-50ng/μL) using the Qubit

**Keep all reagents on magnetic beads from the -20C, mix aliquots by pipetting or inverting DO NOT VORTEX**

### TruSeq PCR-Free Sample Preparation - Acronyms

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

```{r, echo=FALSE, Warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
Acronyms<-c("SPB","CTE","ERP2","RSB","CTA","ATL","CTL","LIG2","STL")
Definition<-
c("Sample Purification Beads","End Repair Control","End Repair Mix","Resuspension Buffer","A-Tailing Control","A-Tailing Mix","Ligation Control","Ligation Mix","Stop Ligation Buffer")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Acronyms,Definition)) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "bordered", full_width = F, position = "left")
```

</details>

### TruSeq PCR-Free Sample Preparation - Workflow

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

[**1)**]{style="color:#cc0000"} **Fragment DNA**

1.  Transfer 50μL of supernatant from each sample into a Covaris tube. If the glass rod falls out of the Covaris tube- discard the entire tube and get a new one. Closing the tubes can be difficult, ensure that the glass rod is as upright as possible before closing.
2.  Turn on the Covaris and the computer
3.  Open SonoLab 7.2 and select the method: TruSeq PCR-free HS (550bp)
4.  Fill the chamber with milliQ water until water goes into the overflow chamber located to the right of the main chamber.
5.  Lower the square handle and close the door.
6.  Check to make sure there are all green check marks in the Instrument status window under Status.
7.  Open the door and insert a Covaris tube with sample, lower the square handle, and close the door.
8.  Make sure all of the green check marks are still on the screen.
9.  Click Run.
10. Repeat this for all samples, once finished close out of the program and shut down both the computer and the instrument.
11. Using a 1000μL pipette- pipette out all of the water from the chamber you can remove the chamber insert to get the rest of the water out, just make sure to put it back when you are done. If necessary use a Kimwipe to get any last bit of water.
12. Close the door.
13. Transfer sonicated samples from the covaris tubes to a bead cleaning plate.

[**2)**]{style="color:#cc0000"} **Clean Up Fragment DNA**

1.  Vortex SPB until well-dispersed\

2.  Add 80μL SPB to each well, pipette up and down to mix\

3.  Incubate the plate at room temperature for 5 minutes\

4.  Place the plate on the magnetic stand until the liquid is clear (\~2-3min)\

5.  Remove and discard all supernatant from each well\

6.  Wash two times as follows:

    i)  Make 80% EtOH fresh and add 200μL to each well\
    ii) Incubate on the magnetic stand for 30 seconds\
    iii) Remove and discard all supernatant\
         \

7.  Use a p20 or p10 to remove any remaining EtOH\

8.  Dry the samples until the beads appear cracked (\~5-10min)\

9.  Remove the plate from the magnetic stand\

10. Add 1.5μL RSB to each well\

11. Pipette up and down to resuspend the beads\

12. Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes\

13. Place on the magnetic stand and wait until the liquid is clear (\~2-3min)\

14. Transfer 50μL of supernatat to a 1.2mL PCR tube or 8-strip tube depending on how many samples you are working with.

[**3)**]{style="color:#cc0000"} **Repair Ends and Select Library Size**

1.  Add 10μL of **CTE** to each sample\

2.  Add 40μL of **ERP2** to each sample\

3.  Pipette up and down to mix\

4.  Place on Thermocycler and run the following protocol: turseq erp

5.  Remove samples from the Thermocycler once the protocol is complete and transfer the samples to a bead cleaning plate\

6.  Make the following dilution of the SPB:

    (\# of samples x 92μL of SPB) + (\# of samples x 92μL of H2O)

7.  Vortex the SPB dilution until the beads are well-dispersed\

8.  Add 160μL of diluted SPB to each sample, pipette up and down to mix\

9.  Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes\

10. Place the plate on the magnetic stand until the liquid is clear (\~5min)

11. Transfer 250μL of supernatant to a new well on the bead the cleaning plate\

12. Discard any remaining diluted SPB\

13. Vortex undiluted SPB until well-dispersed\

14. Add 30μL undiluted SPB to each well, pipette to mix\

15. Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes\

16. Place the plate on the magnetic stand until the liquid is clear (\~2-3min)\

17. Discard all supernatant\

18. Wash two times as follows:

    i)  Make 80% EtOH fresh and add 200μL to each well\
    ii) Incubate on the magnetic stand for 30 seconds\
    iii) Remove and discard all supernatant\
         \

19. Use a p20 or p10 to remove any remaining EtOH\

20. Allow the plate to dry until the beads appear cracked\

21. Remove the plate from the magnetic stand\

22. Add 1.5μL of RSB and pipette to re-suspend the beads\

23. Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes\

24. Place the plate on the magnetic stand\

25. Transfer 15μL of supernatant to a 0.2mL PCR tube or 8-strip tube *depending on how many samples you are working with*

This is a safe stopping point- place all samples in the -20C for up to 7 days

[**4)**]{style="color:#cc0000"} **Adenylate 3' Ends**

1.  Add 2.5μL of CTA to each sample\
2.  Add 12.5μL of ATL to each sample\
3.  Pipette up and down to mix\
4.  Place samples on Thermocycler and run the following protocol: truseq.atail70

[**4)**]{style="color:#cc0000"} **Ligate Adapters**

1.  Add 2.5μL CTL\
2.  Add 2.5μL LIG2\
3.  Add 2.5μL DNA Adapters\
4.  Pipette up and down to mix\
5.  Place samples on the Thermocycler and run the following protocol: truseq.lig\
6.  Add 5μL STL\
7.  Pipette to mix\
8.  Transfer samples to a bead cleaning plate

[**4)**]{style="color:#cc0000"} **Clean Up Ligated Fragments**

1.  Vortex SPB until well-dispersed\

2.  Add 42.5μL SPB to each sample and pipette to mix\

3.  Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes\

4.  Place the plate on the magnetic stand and wait for liquid to clear (\~2-3min)\

5.  Remove and discard all supernatant\

6.  Wash two times as follows:

    i)  Make 80% EtOH fresh and add 200μL to each well\
    ii) Incubate on the magnetic stand for 30 seconds\
    iii) Remove and discard all supernatant\

7.  Use a p20 or p10 to remove any remaining EtOH\

8.  Allow the plate to dry until the beads appear cracked\

9.  Remove the plate from the magnetic stand\

10. Add 52.5μL of RSB to each well, pipette to mix\

11. Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes\

12. Place the plate on the magnetic stand and wait for the liquid to clear (\~2-3min)\

13. Transfer 50μL of supernatant to a clean well on the bead cleaning plate\

14. Vortex SPB until well-dispersed\

15. Add 50μL SPB to each sample and pipette to mix\

16. Incubate at room temperature for 5 minutes\

17. Place the plate on the magnetic stand and wait for liquid to clear (\~2-3min)\

18. Remove and discard all supernatant\

19. Wash two times as follows:

    i)  Make 80% EtOH fresh and add 200μL to each well\
    ii) Incubate on the magnetic stand for 30 seconds\
    iii) Remove and discard all supernatant\

20. Use a p20 or p10 to remove any remaining EtOH\

21. Allow the plate to dry until the beads appear cracked\

22. Remove the plate from the magnetic stand\

23. Add 22.5μL of RSB to each well, pipette to mix\

24. Incubate at room temperature for 2 minutes\

25. Place the plate on the magnetic stand and wait for the liquid to clear (\~2-3min)\

26. Transfer 20μL of supernatant to a 0.5mL tube

Do not concentrate samples to \~1.7ng/μL- take a reading using the Qubit and record the concentration, store samples in the -20C in the Final Genomes Box

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Nextera DNA Flex Library Preparation

### Nextera DNA Flex Library Preparation Acronyms

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

```{r, echo=FALSE, Warning=FALSE, results='asis'}
Acronyms<-c("SPB","TSB","TWB","TB1","EPM","BLT","RSB")
Definition<-
c("Sample Purification Beads","Tagment Stop Buffer","Tagment Wash Buffer","Tagmentation Buffer 1","Enhanced PCR Mix","Bead-Linked Transposomes","Resuspension Buffer")
knitr::kable(data.frame(Acronyms,Definition)) %>% 
  kableExtra::kable_styling(bootstrap_options = "bordered", full_width = F, position = "left")
```

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

### Nextera DNA Flex Library Preparation-Workflow

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

*The products previously known as IDT for Illumina Nextera DNA Unique Dual Indexes Sets A and B (Cat. No. 20027213 and 20027214) are now called IDT for Illumina DNA/RNA UD Indexes Sets A and B*

------------------------------------------------------------------------

***Handling Bead Linked Transposomes (BLT)***

-   If beads are aspirated into pipette tips, dispense back into the plate on the magnetic stand and wait until the liquid is clear (\~2 minutes).

-   Dispense tagment wash buffer (TWB) directly onto the beads.

-   If beads are adhered to the side or top of a 96-well plate, centrifuge at 280 × g for 3 seconds, and then pipette to resuspend

-   *When washing beads:* If liquid becomes adhered to the side or top of the tube or well, centrifuge at 280 × g for 3 seconds to pull volume into liquid.

***Handling Tagment Wash Buffer (TWB)***

-   Pipette slowly to minimize foaming

***Before beginning***:

-   Remove BLT aliquot(s) from fridge, bring to room temperature, vortex vigorously to mix. **DO NOT CENTRIFUGE OR SPIN**

-   Remove TB1 aliquot(s) from -20C, bring to room temperature, vortex to mix

------------------------------------------------------------------------

**Tagment Genomic DNA:**

1.  Add 30μL of gDNA to a plate within a 50-500ng range.\
    If volume of DNA is \<30μL add nuclease-free water to bring volume to 30μL

2.  Make sure BLT is well mixed, combine 11μL BTL and 11μL TB1 **for each sample**, vortex the master mix, then transfer 20μL master mix to each well\
    *For more than 4 samples, divide master mix volume evenly into an 8 strip tube, and use a multi-channel pipete to transfer 20uL of master mix into each well containing a sample*

3.  Seal plate and place on thermocycler, run the program **NXT FLX TAG**

**Post Tagmentation Cleanup**

1.  Add 10μL TSB to each well, slowly pipette the entire volume to resuspend beads

2.  Seal the plate and place on thermocycler, run the program **NXT FLX POST**

3.  Place the plate on the magnet and wait until solution is clear *(\~3minutes)*, discard supernatant

4.  Wash twice as follows:\

<!-- -->

i)  Remove plate from magnet and add 100μL TWB onto beads\
ii) Pipette slowly to minimize foaming, fully resuspend beads\
iii) Place the plate on the magnet and wait until solution is clear *(\~3 minutes)*, discard supernatant

<!-- -->

1.  Remove plate from magnet and add 100μL TWB, pipette slowly to resuspend beads

2.  Seal the plate and place on magnet stand until step 11

3.  Remove EPM aliquot(s) from -20C, thaw on ice, invert to mix and briefly centrifuge

4.  Remove index adapters from -20C, thaw at room temperature, vortex briefly to mix

5.  Prepare PCR master mix in 1.5mL tube by combining 22μL EPM and 22μL Nuclease-free water for each sample, vortex to mix

6.  With plate on magnet discard supernatant, remove plate from magnet. Immediately add 40μL PCR master mix to each well

7.  Add appropriate index adapters to each sample, pipette to mix

8.  Seal the plate and centrifuge briefly, place the plate on thermocycler and run the program NXT FLX PCR

9.  Remove plate from PCR when the program completes and centrifuge briefly

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Sequencing

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Sample Sheet

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

1.  In the LIMS, navigate to the Sequence Book\
    (LIMS$\rightarrow$Workflow$\rightarrow$Sequences)

    -   Enter the Run date as **YYYYMMDD**\
    -   Enter the Sequencing Run ID as SIDYY\#\#\#\
    -   Enter the Flowcell ID and Reagent Cartridge Number\
    -   Click 'Save'\
        \

2.  In the LIMS, navigate to the Sample Sheet page\
    (LIMS$\rightarrow$ Reports/Templates$\rightarrow$Sample Sheet)

    -   Find and select your Sequencing Run ID\
    -   Select the correct flow cell\
        (if the Sequencing Run was named correctly, the flowcell ID should match with the 5 middle alphanumeric values)\
    -   click *Create Template*\
        \

3.  Export the Sample Sheet and go through it to make sure there are:

    i)  **No spaces, periods, dashes, or underscores**\

    ii) All samples have **unique Sample Names and Sample IDs**
    
    iii) Check that there are **no duplicate indexes** by concatenating the forward and reverse in a separate column, then apply conditional formatting to highlight duplicates

        -   Forgetting to check through the sample sheet can cause issues for the MiSeq during the Indexing QC\
            \

4.  Once you are sure that the sample sheet is correct, save the Sample Sheet to [**(Z:MarsData/SeqSampleSheet)**]{style="color:#4d53da"}

    -   **Make sure to close out the csv after saving**; if it is still open on your computer, the file will not correctly upload on the sequencer

> **Notes**: The reagent cartridge can be thawed either in the -20C for at least a day or in a cold water bath for at least an hour (use the tub below CGI's sink).

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Sequencing Sample Prep Workflow

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

1.  Remove a 500 cycle reagent cartridge from the -20°C freezer.\
    Place in room temperature water bath for 1 hour.\
    Place HT1 buffer tube in 4°C fridge

2.  Prepare fresh 0.1N NaOH by diluting the provided 25μL 2N NaOH aliquots with 225μL of nuclease free H~2~O and vortex.

3.  Denature and dilute 16S library and any other libraries.

    All similar samples - 16S, genomes, etc - should be combined according to the number of samples in each single library\
    (i.e. if a library has 37 samples, 3.7μL should be added to the 4nM pooled libraries tube- do not add less than a micro-liter).\
    Keep these libraries separate until the final loading of the reagent cartridge.

    i)  Mix 5μL of 4nM library with 5μL of NaOH, vortex, and spin down. Incubate at RT for 5 minutes\
    ii) Add 990μL HT1 and vortex.\
        *This library is now at 20pM and is good for three weeks if stored at -20C*\
        \
        
    **Heat Denature protocol** (for use when necessary)
      i) Turn on thermomixer prior to denaturation to warm up. Settings: 96C, 0 RPM
      
      ii) Prepare ice bath
      
      iii) Immediately after adding HT1, place pool on thermomixer at 96C for 2 minutes
      
      iv) Invert tube twice and then place in ice bath for 5 minutes

4.  Adjust and denature PhiX.

    i)  Mix 2μL 10nM PhiX (aliquot) and 3μL of Tris-Tween (10mM Tris-Cl pH8.5 with 0.1% Tween 20)\
        Vortex and spin down\
    ii) Mix 5μL of 4nM PhiX with 5μL of 0.1N NaOH, vortex, and spin down\
        Incubate at RT for 5 minutes\ *This can be done simultaneously with pooled libraries*
    iii) Add 990μL HT1 and vortex\
         *The PhiX is now diluted to 20pM and is good for \~3 weeks if stored at -20C*\
         \

5.  Adjust amplicon library to 6pM by combining 300μL of the 20pM amplicon library with 700μL of HT1

    i)  Adjust the genome library to 8pM by combining 400μL of the 20pM genome library with 600μL of HT1
    ii) Adjust PhiX to 8pM by combining 400μL of 20pM PhiX with 600μL of HT1\
        \

6.  ***In a strictly 16S sequencing run, we use 30% PhiX per run***

    Add 300μL of PhiX to a tube containing 700μL of 16S library, vortex, and chill on ice until ready to load into reagent cartridge.\
    This proportion of PhiX changes with diversity of samples or the inclusion of genomes.\
    \
    *A minimum of 1% PhiX should always be run during sequencing.\
    A full genome run is up to 12 genomes.\
    Final sequencing library should be in desired ratio, to a total volume of 1mL.*

7.  When the reagent cartridge has thawed, dry bottom with a paper towel.\
    Carefully invert the cartridge repeatedly to check each well is thawed, making sure to create as little bubbles as possible. This also serves to mix the reagents.\
    Place in fridge until ready to load.

8.  Using a clean 1000μL pipette tip in each, pierce the foil covering wells 12, 13, 14, and 17 of the reagent cartridge, leaving the tip in place.

    i)  Pull up \~140μL from the bottom of Well 12 and add it to Read 1.\
    ii) Transfer the full volume of Read 1 Sequencing Primer to the bottom of well 12 and pipette to mix.\
    iii) Repeat this process spiking the Index Primer into well 13 and the Read 2 Sequencing Primer into well 14.

9.  Pipette 650μL of final library (containing PhiX) into well 17.\
    Place cartridge in fridge until ready to load into MiSeq\
    Unbox flowcell and PR2 bottle

10. Thoroughly rinse the flow cell with DI water. Carefully dry by blotting with Kim wipes\
    Give special attention to the edges and points of intersection between the glass and plastic

11. Using an alcohol wipe, clean the glass on both sides avoiding the rubber intake ports.\
    Completely dry the flowcell with lens paper

12. Visually inspect the flow cell to ensure there are no blemishes, particles, or fibers on the glass.

13. Transfer reagent cartridge, flow cell, PR2 bottle to MiSeq.

    i)  Once the reagent cartridge is read, select the correct Sample Sheet from [**(Z:MarsData/SeqSampleSheet)**]{style="color:#4d53da"}\
        Empty and replace the waste bottle

14. Ensure the machine recognizes the correct sample sheet and the run parameters are correct (specifically the read number)

15. Wait for the MiSeq to perform its pre-run checks and press start\
    *The pre-run checks can take anywhere from 5 minutes to 15 minutes, so make sure you press start before walking away from the MiSeq*

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Run Monitoring

The run should be monitored periodically using Illumina Sequence Analysis Viewer.

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

-   Ideal parameters for a 70% 16S run:

    -   Cluster density 700-800k/mm2 for v2 kits,\
        however acceptable rests can be had with above 600k/mm2 cluster density\
    -   Above 80% clusters passing filter
    -   30% aligned (or percent of total run of PhiX)
    -   Final \>Q30 score of above 80%

</details>

## Post-Run Wash

[*illumina Support Guide for Miseq Washes*](https://support.illumina.com/content/dam/illumina-support/courses/MiSeq_Instrument_Washes/story_content/external_files/MiSeq_Instrument_Washes_Narration_Transcript.pdf)

Perform a **post-run wash** on the MiSeq by clicking *Start Wash* after the run has completed.\
Click the option for a **template-line wash**.\
*The post-run wash takes approximately 20 minutes.*

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

**To prepare fresh 0.5% Tween wash solution**:

1.  Add 5mL of 100% Tween to a 50mL Centrifuge Tube

2.  Add 45mL of water from the Pure Lab Flex filter to the tube and invert several times to mix\
    *Now you have 10% Tween*

3.  Pour 25 mL of the 10% Tween solution into a 500mL bottle marked "0.5% Tween". The rest can be saved on the bench for a later post-run wash.

4.  Add 475mL Pure Lab filter water to the 500mL bottle marked "0.5% Tween."
  
    **This solution should be added to either the squirt bottle labelled "0.5% Tween 20 for MiSeq Wash" or the 500mL Wash Bottle**

**0.5% Tween is already made**:

1.  Remove the spent reagent cartridge and the bottle with excess buffer solution.\
    Flush the buffer down the drain while running cold water\
    Empty the waste container and put it back

    **DO NOT DUMP THE REAGENT WASTE DOWN THE DRAIN OR PLACE IN THE TRASH!**\
    The reagent waste in cartridge well 8 must be disposed of in the specially marked container found in the Satellite Waste Area:

    -   Use the syringe next to the sink to remove as much liquid as possible from the spent cartridge and place in a secondary waste container.
    -   Dispose of the liquid waste in the formaldehyde waste jug found in the Satellite Accumulation Area\
    -   Place the spent reagent cartridge in the waste basket.\
    -   Leave flow cell in place until next sequencing run.\
        \

2.  Fill each well of the wash resevoir with \~6ml wash solution (does not have to be exact)\
    *wash solution is 0.5% Tween*\
    **Leave well 17 empty**

3.  Fill the 500ml wash bottle with 350ml wash solution and place into the MiSeq

4.  Make a fresh dilute bleach solution and add to the wash reservoir in well 17

    -   Add 38μL 5.25% Bleach to 962μL MilliQ water and vortex to mix\
        *This makes a \~0.2% bleach solution*

5.  Add 50μL 0.2% bleach solution to Reservoir 17\
    **Be sure to use the plastic resevoir liner, kept on the sink in the sequencing room**

6.  Add 950μL of MilliQ water to Reservoir 17 and pipette to mix

7.  Place the wash cartridge into the chiller, empty and replace the waste container and begin the wash.

</details>

------------------------------------------------------------------------

## Sequence Results

<details>

<summary>

</summary>

When MiSeq Reporter finishes, copy the "DemultiplexSummaryF1L1.txt" from the Data/Intensities/Basecalls/Alignment folder on the MiSeq to (Z:/MarsData/SequenceResults)

1.  To calculate the number of reads per sample, open up the Demultiplexing file that was copied over to SequenceResults.

    -   On BaseSpace, navigate to the run you are resulting and click "FastQ Generation"
    -   Click on "View Files" in the middle of the screen next to "Logs"
    -   Select the "DemultiplexSummaryF1L1.txt"

2.  Insert a row below the sample names (Row 2).

3.  Take the average of the values below the sample name.\
    These are the decimal values that are in the same rows as "s_1\_1101" to "s_1\_2114".

4.  Multiply this average with PF Reads (found under Run Details Indexing QC) and then divide this by 200.\
    -   In BaseSpace, click on the "Stats.json" file and copy the number of total clusters pass filter to paste into cell B03.
    *Because Illumina has changed the number of PF reads under Indexing QC from the number of clusters to the number of reads, you now have to divide the number of PF Reads by 200 instead of 100.*\
    The number of clusters per sample should reflect this.
    
    *You can also copy the function from a previous Demux Summary spreadsheet found in **Z: MarsData/SequenceResults***

    This will give you the total number of reads for each sample. Ex. For the first sample (found in cell C2),

5.  Copy and paste the values back into the cells after the calculation is complete.

6.  In the LIMS under Tools, click CSV Batch Upload Tool. Download the CSV for Sequence Results.

7.  Copy both the Sample Names and Values from the Demultiplexing calculation and use "transpose" and "values" to paste them into the csv you just downloaded.

8.  Fill in the Sequencing Run ID into the first column of the Sequence Results csv and upload that file to the LIMS.

</details>
